Servers must implement proper access controls on tools.
Servers must rate limit tool invocations.
Servers must sanitize tool outputs.
Clients should prompt for user confirmation on sensitive tool operations.
Clients should show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or accidental data exfiltration.
Clients should validate tool results before passing them to the LLM.
Clients should implement timeouts for tool calls.
Clients should log tool usage for audit purposes.
MCP defines a standardized mechanism by which servers offer argument-value autocompletion for prompts (identified by name) and resource templates (identified by URI).
A server that supports completions MUST declare the `completions` capability (an empty object) in its advertised capabilities.
condition: the server offers completion support

statement: Clients request suggestions with a `completion/complete` JSON-RPC request that identifies the completion target via a `ref` and names the `argument` being completed (its `name` and current `value`).
MCP completion supports exactly two reference types: `ref/prompt` (a prompt referenced by name) and `ref/resource` (a resource referenced by URI template).
When a prompt or resource template has multiple arguments, clients should send the already-resolved argument values in `context.arguments` so the server can return context-dependent suggestions.
condition: the target prompt or template has more than one argument

statement: A CompleteRequest carries `ref`, an `argument` object ({name, value}), and an optional `context` whose `arguments` field maps already-resolved argument names to their values.
A CompleteResult returns a `completion` object containing `values` (the ranked suggestions), an optional `total` count of available matches, and a `hasMore` boolean.
A single completion response must contain at most 100 suggestion items.
Servers should return completion values sorted by relevance.
The `total` field is optional and reports the number of available matches, while `hasMore` indicates whether additional results exist beyond those returned.
Servers should implement fuzzy matching for completion suggestions.
condition: fuzzy matching is appropriate for the argument being completed

statement: Servers should rate-limit completion requests.
Clients should debounce rapid successive completion requests.
Clients should cache completion results.
condition: caching is appropriate for the use case

statement: Clients should handle missing or partial completion results gracefully.

For error cases servers should return standard JSON-RPC errors: -32601 when the completions capability is not supported, -32602 for an invalid prompt name or for missing required arguments, and -32603 for internal errors.
Implementations MUST validate all completion inputs.
Implementations MUST apply appropriate rate limiting to completion handling.
Implementations MUST control access to sensitive suggestions so that completions do not expose restricted data.
Implementations MUST prevent completion-based information disclosure (e.g., inferring protected values by probing suggestions).
The protocol does not mandate any specific user-interaction model for completion; implementations are free to expose it through any interface (for example an IDE-style dropdown).
exception: the protocol imposes no required UI pattern, so implementations may choose any presentation

statement: MCP defines a standardized mechanism for servers to send structured log messages to clients.
Clients control logging verbosity by setting a minimum log level.
A server log notification carries a severity level, an optional logger name, and arbitrary JSON-serializable data.
The protocol mandates no specific user-interaction model for logging; an implementation may expose logging through any interface pattern.
A server that emits log-message notifications must declare the `logging` capability.
condition: the server emits log message notifications

statement: Log levels follow the eight RFC 5424 syslog severities: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, and emergency.
A client may set the minimum log level by sending a `logging/setLevel` request.
Servers deliver log messages using `notifications/message` notifications.
Once a minimum log level is configured, the server emits only messages at that level and above.
condition: after the client sets a minimum log level via logging/setLevel

statement: A server should return JSON-RPC error `-32602` (Invalid params) for an invalid log level.
condition: on an invalid log level in a setLevel request

statement: A server should return JSON-RPC error `-32603` (Internal error) for configuration errors.
condition: on a logging configuration error

statement: Servers should rate-limit log messages.
Servers should include relevant context in the log message data field.
Servers should use consistent logger names.
Servers should remove sensitive information from log messages.
Log messages must not contain credentials or secrets.
Log messages must not contain personally identifying information.
Log messages must not contain internal system details that could aid attacks.
Implementations should validate all data fields in log messages.
Implementations should control access to logs.
Implementations should monitor log content for sensitive information.
A client may present, filter, search, visually distinguish severity of, and persist log messages.
MCP supports paginating list operations that may return large result sets, letting servers yield results in smaller chunks rather than all at once.
Pagination is especially important when a server connects to external services over the internet, and is also useful for local integrations to avoid performance issues with large data sets.
condition: connecting to external services over the internet, or working with large data sets

statement: MCP pagination uses an opaque cursor-based approach rather than numbered pages.
A pagination cursor is an opaque string token that represents a position in the result set.
Page size is determined by the server, not the client.
Clients MUST NOT assume a fixed page size.
A paginated response includes the current page of results and an optional nextCursor field, where nextCursor is present only if more results exist.
condition: more results exist beyond the current page

statement: To continue paginating, the client issues a follow-up list request that carries the previously returned cursor in the request's params.cursor field.
condition: a nextCursor was returned by the previous response

statement: The MCP operations that support pagination are resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list, and tools/list.
Servers SHOULD provide stable cursors.
Servers SHOULD handle invalid cursors gracefully.
Clients SHOULD treat a missing nextCursor as the end of the result set.
condition: the response omits nextCursor

statement: Clients SHOULD support both paginated and non-paginated flows.
Clients MUST treat cursors as opaque tokens and MUST NOT make assumptions about cursor format.
Clients MUST NOT attempt to parse or modify cursors.
Clients MUST NOT persist cursors across sessions.
Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params).
condition: the supplied cursor is invalid

statement: MCP protocol versions are date-shaped string identifiers whose date records the most recent backwards-incompatible change.
A protocol revision should not change its version identifier for updates that preserve backwards compatibility.
exception: If an update introduces a backwards-incompatible change, the date identifier advances.

statement: MCP revision status separates in-progress drafts, the usable current revision, and completed final revisions that will not change further.
In the source snapshot, the current MCP protocol revision is 2025-11-25.
condition: For the source snapshot fetched on 2026-07-05.

statement: Deprecated MCP features remain part of the specification while being scheduled for later removal.
condition: When a feature is marked Deprecated.

statement: Deprecated features need an explicit migration path or an explicit statement that no migration is required.
condition: When a feature is marked Deprecated.

statement: A deprecated feature is not eligible for removal until it has remained in the specification for the minimum deprecation window.
condition: When the normal lifecycle applies, the minimum window is twelve months; under expedited removal, the minimum window is ninety days.

statement: MCP clients and servers must negotiate the protocol version during initialization.
A client and server may each implement multiple MCP versions, but a session must use one agreed version.
condition: During a single initialized session.

statement: A client that cannot negotiate a mutually supported MCP version should terminate the connection through the protocol error path rather than proceed ambiguously.
condition: When version negotiation fails.

statement: HTTP implementations for MCP 2025-06-18 and later must include the negotiated protocol version on later HTTP requests using the MCP-Protocol-Version header.
condition: When using HTTP transport after initialization on revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: The 2024-11-05 baseline used the original HTTP plus SSE transport shape rather than Streamable HTTP.
condition: When auditing an implementation negotiated to 2024-11-05.

statement: The 2025-03-26 revision replaced the earlier HTTP plus SSE transport with Streamable HTTP.
condition: When auditing an implementation negotiated to 2025-03-26 or newer.

statement: A Streamable HTTP implementation for 2025-11-25 should return HTTP 403 when an Origin header is invalid.
condition: When auditing Streamable HTTP behavior against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: The 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP behavior allows polling over SSE-style streams and permits server-initiated disconnection.
condition: When auditing polling, resumption, or stream lifetime behavior against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: JSON-RPC batching is conformant only for the 2025-03-26 MCP revision.
condition: When evaluating whether an implementation sends, accepts, emits, or requires JSON-RPC batches.
exception: It is not conformant for 2024-11-05 or for 2025-06-18 and later revisions.

statement: The 2025-03-26 revision added an OAuth 2.1 based authorization framework to MCP.
condition: When comparing 2025-03-26 against 2024-11-05.

statement: The 2025-06-18 revision treats MCP servers as OAuth Resource Servers and adds protected-resource metadata for discovering the relevant authorization server.
condition: When auditing authorization against revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: MCP clients for 2025-06-18 and later must use RFC 8707 Resource Indicators to protect token audience handling.
condition: When auditing client authorization behavior against revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: The 2025-11-25 revision expands authorization support with OpenID Connect discovery, incremental scope consent, OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents, and RFC 9728 alignment.
condition: When auditing authorization against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: The 2025-03-26 revision added tool annotations for describing tool behavior such as read-only or destructive operation.
condition: When comparing 2025-03-26 against 2024-11-05.

statement: The 2025-06-18 revision added structured tool output and resource links in tool call results.
condition: When auditing tool-result behavior against revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: Input validation failures in 2025-11-25 tool calls should be reported as Tool Execution Errors instead of Protocol Errors so the model can correct the call.
condition: When auditing tool-call error classification against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: MCP elicitation support first appears in 2025-06-18 and is expanded in 2025-11-25 with URL-mode elicitation, more standards-based result and enum schemas, and primitive default values.
condition: When auditing server-to-user elicitation behavior.

statement: The 2024-11-05 baseline content types are text and image, while audio support is added in 2025-03-26.
condition: When auditing supported content types by negotiated revision.

statement: The 2025-06-18 revision adds a title field so human-facing display names can be separated from programmatic names.
condition: When auditing naming or display metadata against revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: The 2025-11-25 revision adds metadata support for icons on tools, resources, resource templates, and prompts.
condition: When auditing user-facing metadata against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: The 2025-11-25 revision adds tool-calling support to sampling through tool-selection parameters.
condition: When auditing sampling features against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: The 2025-06-18 lifecycle operation requirement is mandatory rather than advisory.
condition: When auditing lifecycle behavior against revision 2025-06-18 or newer.

statement: MCP schema definitions default to JSON Schema 2020-12 in the 2025-11-25 revision.
condition: When auditing schema dialect assumptions against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: The 2025-11-25 revision introduces experimental tasks for durable requests with polling and deferred result retrieval.
condition: When auditing task-like durable request support against revision 2025-11-25.

statement: A version audit should establish the negotiated MCP version before judging any transport, authorization, tool, schema, or lifecycle behavior.
A version audit should match the implementation transport to the negotiated revision and verify which transport the server advertises when multiple transports exist in code.
condition: When an implementation appears to support more than one transport shape.

statement: Authorization review should be performed against the specific negotiated revision because MCP authorization requirements changed across 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, and 2025-11-25.
condition: When auditing token audience handling, resource metadata, server discovery, scope consent, or client registration.

statement: A server on the current revision can still legitimately expose deprecated-but-present features during the applicable deprecation window.
condition: When a feature is deprecated but has not yet reached its removal eligibility window.
